=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2533-2544 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The follow-up lineage extractors parse the raw issue body, so fenced or quoted diagnostic content can supply authoritative branch declarations.
  WHY: An attacker-controlled branch can redirect the review-blocked follow-up workflow instead of using the verified PR base.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2895-2918 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The reissue metadata extractor searches for the Orchestrator metadata footer without checking whether it is inside a Markdown fence.
  WHY: Fenced diagnostic content can spoof reissue lineage, local ID, and priority settings.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2789 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Fence detection counts backtick and tilde delimiters together, so mixed fence delimiters can make a footer inside an unclosed fence appear authoritative.
  WHY: The parser can extract an attacker-controlled branch from a fake footer inside fenced diagnostic content. The identical pattern appears in scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:22-24, scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:53-55 and 107-109, and .github/workflows/validate.yml:218-219.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:575-576 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: A non-object branch-ref API response can cause an AttributeError while accessing branch.get("object", {}).get("sha").
  WHY: An unexpected API response structure can crash the checker process instead of reporting a clean failed state or raising a ReadError.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:2503-2518 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The test function name claims parent metadata wins over the PR base, but its docstring and assertions verify that the PR base wins over mismatched parent metadata.
  WHY: This is a misleading contract-test name, not a runtime failure. Severity disagreement: NIT (deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2) versus MAJOR (minimax_minimax-m3); the highest severity is used.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py: line 2505, function test_merge_with_followup_parent_metadata_wins_over_pr_base_branch | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function name asserts that parent metadata wins over PR base branch, but the modified test body at lines 2516-2518 now verifies the opposite: PR base (#9999) overrides mismatched parent metadata (#4001).
  WHY: Does not fail at runtime — this is a maintainability hazard. A future reader who searches for this test by name will expect parent-metadata-first behavior and will be misled.
- Requirement: The linked issue #4605 finding validate-generated-issue-base-spoofing requires that branch declarations be accepted only from the leading metadata or an unfenced, separator-delimited Orchestrator metadata footer. Fenced/quoted diagnostic content must not be treated as authoritative. The review-blocked judge serves as an additional incomplete sibling path: its extractors at scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2533-2544 parse the unfiltered FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY (the full issue body) without excluding fenced or diagnostic content, and lines 2894-2918 search for **Orchestrator metadata** in the unfiltered body without verifying the footer is outside a fence. The merge_with_followup path at lines 2549-2567 accepts any valid-looking parent branch without cross-checking it against the independently fetched PR_BASE_REF.
  Expected change site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh lines 2532-2567 (merge_with_followup extractors and cross-check) and lines 2894-2918 (reissue metadata extractor)
  Evidence of absence: The file scripts/review_rb_judge.sh is absent from both pr_changed_files.txt and last_run_changed_files.txt. The last run added five new tests in tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py that expect filtered behavior: test_close_and_reissue_ignores_fenced_orchestrator_footer (line 782), test_merge_with_followup_ignores_fenced_tracking_lineage (line 2521), test_merge_with_followup_does_not_inherit_diagnostic_tracking_issue (line 2533), test_merge_with_followup_strips_judge_prose_lineage (line 2544), and the modified test_merge_with_followup_parent_metadata_wins_over_pr_base_branch (line 2505) and test_merge_with_followup_ignores_default_branch_sentinel (line 2475). At least three of these tests will fail against current production code because the extractors at lines 2533-2544 still use re.MULTILINE on the raw FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY and the extractor at line 2899 still searches the unfiltered body for the footer. Earlier-parser fixes that landed in the original PR diff for resolve_integration_ref.sh, orchestrate_lib.py, orchestrate_force_tick.sh, and validate.yml all include the exact authoritative-metadata filtering that scripts/review_rb_judge.sh still omits.
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: lines 2533-2544 (within extractors for RB_FOLLOWUP_INTEGRATION_BRANCH/RB_FOLLOWUP_TRACKING_ISSUE) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The lineage extractors search the raw FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY without restricting parsing to the authoritative metadata section.
  WHY: Fenced diagnostic content or quoted issue bodies containing spoofed integration branches can be misinterpreted as authoritative, potentially redirecting the review-blocked follow-up workflow to an attacker-controlled branch instead of the verified PR base.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: line 2899 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The extractor for RB_REISSUE_PARENT_ORCH_METADATA_LINES searches the full body for **Orchestrator metadata** without verifying if the marker is inside a Markdown fence.
  WHY: An attacker can include diagnostic content within a fence that mimics the Orchestrator metadata footer, allowing spoofing of reissue lineage, local ID, and priority settings.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: lines 575-576 | severity=HIGH | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A non-object branch-ref API response can cause an AttributeError while accessing branch.get("object", {}).get("sha").
  WHY: An unexpected API response or unexpected JSON structure can crash the checker process instead of reporting a clean failed state or raising a ReadError.
- Requirement: "Read branch declarations only in the leading metadata (before the first section heading, fence, or separator) or the canonical **Orchestrator metadata** footer. Never use a quoted line, check log, or diagnostic as a base." (Ref: issue #4605, consensus finding "The follow-up lineage extractors can accept Integration branch and Tracking issue declarations from fenced or diagnostic content.")
  Expected change site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2532-2590 (merge_with_followup path) and :2894-2956 (reissue metadata path)
  Evidence of absence: The extractors at lines 2533-2538 and 2539-2544 search the raw FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY without restricting to the authoritative metadata section. The extractor at lines 2894-2918 searches for the canonical footer in the full body without verifying it is outside a fence. Other parsers modified in this PR have already implemented the metadata restriction (skipping headings/fences), but these specific review_rb_judge.sh parsers remain vulnerable despite the commit message claiming otherwise.
  severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
- Requirement: "Bind the base to authenticated, machine-generated metadata for the source issue and its triggering PR or run. Reject branch declarations in diagnostic or quoted content, and require the final PR base to match that independent binding." (Ref: issue #4605, consensus finding "Bind the base to authenticated, machine-generated metadata...")
  Expected change site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh merge_with_followup branch logic.
  Evidence of absence: The merge_with_followup path independently reads PR_BASE_REF but does not cross-check parent-extracted lineage against it. If the extractor pulls a branch from fenced diagnostic content, the branch is used without verifying it equals the independently fetched PR base, unlike the close_and_reissue path which performs this cross-check.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py: test_merge_with_followup_parent_metadata_wins_over_pr_base_branch at lines 2503-2518 (renamed assertion contract) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function name claims "parent_metadata_wins_over_pr_base_branch", but the modified assertions and the new docstring ("A mismatched parent declaration cannot replace the independently verified PR base") verify the OPPOSITE: PR base wins over mismatched parent metadata (`assert "- Tracking issue: #9999" in body`, `assert "project-4001" not in body`).
  WHY: Test will still pass mechanically (assertions are correct), but the misleading name will cause future maintainers to either (a) "fix" the assertions to match the name and reintroduce the spoofing defect, or (b) leave the test as a confusing contradiction that obscures the verified contract.
